title: Russell US Style indexes — conditional recapping effective at the open (24% / 4.8%-above-48% test struck on the 2026-12-28 close), the year-end instance the owner's own guide now calls MONTH-end
source: EST: owner-published, re-fetched and re-extracted independently this session from FOUR documents (two live, two archived). (1) FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions -- Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 content streams inflated 2026-09-08 -- byte count reproduces what both siblings recorded). Its dated four-column schedule table's DECEMBER 2026 column reads verbatim "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Cut-Off Date | 28 December 2026" and "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Effective Date (open of, if applicable) | 31 December 2026", and -- THE ROW THE PROPOSAL COULD NOT VERIFY -- "Russell US Style Capping Cut-Off Date | 2 December 2026" with "Review Effective Date (open of) | 14 December 2026". (2) FTSE Russell, "Capping Methodology Guide", v5.4, September 2026 (capping-methodology-guide.pdf, HTTP 200, 652,008 bytes, 62 streams inflated), which states the standing rule in its section 4.8.6 table: reference date "T-3", trigger "No company is greater than 24%, and all companies that have a weight greater than 4.8% in aggregate are no more than 48% of the index", scheme "Rule 4.2/RIC 22.5/45". THE T-3 RULE REPRODUCES THE PUBLISHED DECEMBER DATES EXACTLY, and this is the holiday-aware case worth stating: the last business day of 2026 is Thu 31 December, so T-1 is Wed 30 December, T-2 is Tue 29 December and T-3 is Mon 28 December -- stepping over Christmas Day (Fri 25 December) -- the owner's own published cut-off to the day. THE MATERIAL CORRECTION THIS SESSION FOUND, and the reason two archived versions were pulled: in v5.4 (and in v5.3, August 2026, recovered from web.archive.org 2026-09-02 and inflated in-session) EVERY Russell US Style row in that table reads frequency "Monthly" and effective date "Last business day of each month" -- NOT quarterly. Only the two FTSE Emerging ex China rows, two lines above them, read "Quarterly" / "Last business day in Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec". In v5.2, June 2026 (web.archive.org 2026-06-26, inflated in-session) the same Russell rows read "Last business day in Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec" and the table carried no frequency column at all. So the check went QUARTERLY -> MONTHLY between the June and August 2026 editions of the guide, and the July 2026 FAQ -- which still says verbatim "The review is conducted quarterly (March, June, September, and December)" -- predates the change. The two owner documents genuinely disagree; the guide is the methodology of record, is two months newer, and is the document the FAQ itself points to. Filed estimate on the same three counts as every entry in this family: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for an index owner's own published methodology, this lane may not self-confirm, and the FAQ carries "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes." Conditional by construction -- the guide says "If no breach is identified, no changes are made." Canonical file written by this event's own initial research after reading in full the single proposal carrying this id, checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-08), which read proposals/russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31.from-russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30.json in full first, then re-fetched every owner document rather than inheriting the proposal's readings. Ledger: docs/research/events/russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31.md. THE PROPOSAL ASKED ONE EXPLICIT QUESTION AND THE ANSWER IS NO. It flagged as "NOT YET VERIFIABLE FROM THIS SESSION" whether the Q4 reset that defuses this test falls where the September geometry would put it. It does not. The FAQ's December column publishes the style capping cut-off at 2 December and the review effective open at 14 December, against a quarter-end test struck on the 28 December close -- 17 trading sessions from cut-off to test, where September's 09-09 -> 09-25 leg was 12. That 42% longer drift window is the single number that separates this instance from its sibling, and it roughly DOUBLES the measured breach probability: re-running the sibling's method on this session's own 5-year bar set, a 45%-reset cohort clears the 48% trigger in 96 of 1,237 rolling 17-session windows (7.76%) against 49 of 1,242 rolling 12-session windows (3.95%). The 12-session figure reproduces the sibling's 50/1,243 = 4.02% to within one window, which is the cross-check that the method was re-implemented rather than copied. SECOND FINDING, WHICH CORRECTS THE SIBLING LEDGER: that ledger records the guide as stating the check is effective on the "Last business day in Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec". That is the FTSE Emerging ex China row, two rows above the Russell ones in the same table. Every Russell US Style row in v5.3 (August 2026) and v5.4 (September 2026) reads "Monthly" / "Last business day of each month"; v5.2 (June 2026) read the quarterly wording. The event's own NAME is therefore a legacy label -- 31 December 2026 is the December MONTH-end instance of a monthly check that happens to coincide with quarter-end -- and the calendar is missing eight instances a year on this family. Two were proposed in the same PR (russell-style-month-end-capping-effective-2026-10-30 and -2026-11-30); the rest were declined for want of a published 2027 calendar. THE FREQUENCY CHANGE DOES NOT MOVE THIS EVENT'S OWN NUMBER, and that is stated so nobody reads the correction as a re-pricing: the December quarterly capping review on 2 December already binds the drift window, so an October or November firing would only re-reset a cohort the 12-02 review resets anyway. It changes what the calendar tracks, not what this date is worth. SCOPE AND SIZE, RE-VERIFIED NOT INHERITED: the iShares product screener read this session returns IWF $126.03B, IWD $84.06B, IWP $19.63B, IWY $15.94B, IWS $15.67B, IWO $14.70B, IWN $14.61B, IWX $3.98B = $294.62B, reproducing the sibling's total. IWY's over-4.8% company cohort (Alphabet's two lines combined per the guide's own rule) reads 46.81% and IWF's 44.47% on holdings dated 2026-08-27 -- both within a rounding step of the sibling's 46.79%/44.62%, read from a different source. The single-name leg is dead by a wide margin (NVDA 16.21% in IWY against a 22.5% cap and a 24% trigger). A fired recap still moves about 3pp of IWY's $15.94B, roughly $478M, across five mega caps that each trade multiples of that before lunch. Impact low and symbols deliberately EMPTY on the same measured grounds as the Q3 entry: no house playbook is index-flow-keyed (trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-grepped this session for rebalanc|reconstitution|russell|capping|index.flow|IWF|IWY -> zero hits in both), and an ETF proxy in symbols would make the deterministic screen trip on mega-cap beta. Kind sector matches the family. THE PREDECESSOR IS ALREADY ON THE BOARD: russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11's own title carries "effective at the open 2026-12-14", which is the FAQ's Review Effective Date for the capping review to the day -- two entries filed by different lanes from different documents agreeing on one date.
